notes: Ported from tests/control-undo-structural.py (the structural-undo transcript, feature row 75 / task #664): the fixture is OPENED FROM A COPY (@fixture: copies it out of the tree before any command can write to it), then a track with a clip and three notes is built, its music is removed with track.remove, ONE control.undo must bring the CLIP AND ITS NOTES back - asserted against the clip's content, never against 'a track with that name exists again', which a lossy undo also satisfies - then control.redo re-does the deletion, and the refusals family closes the case. Measured on this build before it was written: the fixture is 1 track / 1 clip on a PATTERN track (its clip has no note list, so roll.get_state on it is a typed refusal - the fixture's own read is kept here), ids are session-ordinal (trk-27, clip-28 on a fresh session), and the restored clip keeps its id, which is what lets @id:drums_clip be rolled after the undo.
